data.ruling: The refutation stands. The row 'watchdog stall cover (V2)' gives the longest legitimate stall found for V2 as 900 ms. That value is finite, and the V2 finding sets no finite bound. The 900 ms holds only for one main-loop pass while the host has stopped reading. For a host that keeps accepting data more slowly than it is written, the finding states 'no bound'. The finding also names a boot pass that erases up to 2 sectors: 800 ms plus prints, if the watchdog is already running by then. The row states neither condition. A timeout just above 900 ms therefore does not cover every stall V2 found. The row is weaker than its source. 'watchdog window (V1 and V2)' is built on it and carries the same error. The second point also holds, as a minor one: the 'PIO blocks and reach' row leaves out IOBoard.md:107's condition that a block 'changes the base only while it holds no program'. Both points concern this function's requirement values, not the part. The RP2354B itself is not refuted by either.
data.evidence: V2 as found, FU-A1 P2-R1 return (results/.../round1/FU-A1/002-P2-R1.json, found_values[1], read_at 2026-09-28T17:14:35Z), quoted: '900 ms for one main-loop pass with a host that stops reading; no bound with a host that keeps accepting data more slowly than it is written ... Each accepted write restarts the 500 ms, so a slow host sets no bound. The boot pass erases up to OUT_STORE_SECTORS = 2 sectors ... 800 ms plus prints, if the watchdog is already running then.' Research.md:562 in checkout e13f5f60 still marks V2 'for research (owner, 2026-09-28)', so no owner answer replaces the finding. pico-sdk 2.3.1 stdio_usb.c, re-read 2026-09-29T01:44:14Z. In stdio_usb_out_chars(), the loop runs until all `length` bytes are written. After each accepted write (n > 0) it sets `last_avail_time = time_us_64();`. It breaks early only if `!tud_cdc_write_available() && time_us_64() > last_avail_time + PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US`. stdio_usb.h:31-33 sets the default to 500000 us. A host that accepts some bytes within every 500 ms therefore keeps the call inside the loop past 900 ms. The only limit is the length of the message. Under firmware/ in checkout e13f5f60, grep finds no PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US override and no watchdog_enable or watchdog_update. `git diff --stat 10b0bade34de e13f5f60d2e5 -- firmware/iomcu` is empty, so the finding still describes the code. IOBoard.md:107 reads 'a PIO block sees 32 GPIO from a base of 0 or 16, for all 4 of its state machines, and changes the base only while it holds no program'. The claim's 'PIO blocks and reach' value omits that condition. The watchdog paragraph at IOBoard.md:221 says only that the timeout 'exceeds the longest legitimate stall of the coprocessor, including a W25Q16JV sector erase (400 ms maximum)'. It gives no 900 ms figure. Saved copies: /home/claude/rcbench-research/round1/scratch/FU-A2/adjudicator-R1/stdio_usb-2.3.1.c and stdio_usb-2.3.1.h.
